newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Battered Manila stock market finds a sparkle.
newsitem.headline: Battered Manila stock market finds a sparkle.

text.p: The Philippine stock market roared back to life on Monday after a six-day losing streak but analysts were wary about predicting that the worst was over.
The main index jumped just over five percent to 2,736.42, its highest for just over a week and following some of the sharpest falls in the market for more than two years.
The falls were triggered initially by fears of an impending property crash.

"We did not expect a technical rebound this big, but I say that this has to be sustained for at least a week before we can say with conviction that there has been a reversal," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
"It was a good breather. But we have to wait and see if it could be sustained before we can say that the trend has indeed been reversed," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities Phils Inc.
After days of bad news that had some analysts predicting the Philippine economy might be slowing down, the market on Monday finally had something to cheer about.

Not least was the government announcement that inflation in April had actually fallen, contrary to many predictions of another rise, to 4.6 percent year-on-year compared with 4.8 percent the previous month.
"It's a welcome surprise. The market is getting quite excited about the number," Fiona Paua, research head of Citicorp Securities, said.
It was enough to make some analysts consider lowering their forecasts for the year.

After dire predictions that last week's hammering would continue this week, the share market made a cautious start but by the middle of the morning was steaming up as investors decided some of the leading shares had fallen too far.
Blue chips such as Ayala Corp and Manila Electric Co and including heavily battered Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, carried the index higher.
Traders said the successful listing of movie company Premiere Entertainment Productions set the tone, helped by the inflation figures.
The share debuted at 1.10 pesos, compared with its one peso offer price. By 0615 GMT, the price had risen to 1.26 pesos.

However, nervousness that there could be more speculation against the peso -- already hit as foreign share investors changed their money into dollars -- prompted the Central Bank to increase interest rates for the second time in a week.
It raised its overnight borrowing rate to 11.50 percent from 11.0 percent. ($1 = 26.36 pesos)
